spellbook_fire_spark.name: Spellbook of Fire Spark
spellbook_fire_spark.lore: Zeus hid fire from mankind, and Prometheus stole it back from Olympus inside the pithy stalk of a giant fennel, where an ember will smoulder for hours without burning through. Every apprentice's first fire lesson is a copy of that theft. The spell throws one dart of flame, hot as a candle and about as large.

spellbook_fire_bolt.name: Spellbook of Fire Bolt
spellbook_fire_bolt.lore: The Chimera had a lion's head, a goat's body and a serpent's tail, and it breathed fire over Lycia. Bellerophon flew above it on Pegasus and thrust a lump of lead into its throat on the point of his lance. Its own breath melted the lead and choked it. This primer teaches the breath: one hard bolt of flame.

spellbook_fireball.name: Spellbook of Fireball
spellbook_fireball.lore: Later writers say that when the Roman fleet closed on Syracuse in 212 before Christ, Archimedes lined the walls with polished bronze shields and turned the noon sun onto the ships until their timbers caught. Engineers still argue over whether it could work. The battle-mage's version does. Everything hostile in sight burns at once.

spellbook_meteor.name: Spellbook of Meteor
spellbook_meteor.lore: On 7 November 1492 a stone weighing more than a hundred kilograms fell with a thunderclap into a wheat field outside Ensisheim in Alsace. The townsfolk chained it up inside the church so that it could not leave the way it came. This tome teaches how to call one down. Whatever stands in sight is under it.

spellbook_cataclysm.name: Spellbook of Cataclysm
spellbook_cataclysm.lore: There were five cities on the plain of the Jordan. Abraham bargained for them down to ten righteous men, and ten could not be found. Brimstone and fire rained from heaven, and in the morning he saw smoke going up like the smoke of a furnace. The last fire spell brings down five burning stones in succession.

spellbook_frost_touch.name: Spellbook of Frost Touch
spellbook_frost_touch.lore: In Hans Christian Andersen's tale of 1844, a splinter of a goblin's mirror lodges in a boy's heart and it becomes a lump of ice. The Snow Queen has only to kiss him twice and he no longer feels the cold at all. The first frost lesson is a touch of that sort. It bites, and it sometimes slows.

spellbook_cold_bolt.name: Spellbook of Cold Bolt
spellbook_cold_bolt.lore: The giantess Skadi came down from the mountains in full armour to avenge her father, and the gods bought peace with a husband. She had to choose by feet alone and picked the wrong god. She went home to hunt on skis. This tome teaches her kind of shot: a shard of ice that leaves its mark slow.

spellbook_ice_storm.name: Spellbook of Ice Storm
spellbook_ice_storm.lore: The seventh plague of Egypt was hail, with fire running along the ground among it, the worst since Egypt became a nation. It broke every tree and beat down the flax and the barley in the fields. Only Goshen was spared. The spell is that sky in a single room. Every enemy in sight is under the stones.

spellbook_cone_of_cold.name: Spellbook of Cone of Cold
spellbook_cone_of_cold.lore: Dante expected fire at the bottom of Hell and found ice. Traitors lie frozen in the lake Cocytus to their necks, and at its centre Satan stands locked to the chest, beating six wings whose wind keeps the whole lake hard. The last frost spell is one beat of those wings. Everything close in front freezes solid.

spellbook_spark.name: Spellbook of Spark
spellbook_spark.lore: Sailors in a storm sometimes saw blue fire hiss on the mastheads and took it for the sign of their patron, Saint Erasmus, whom they called Elmo. It meant the worst of the weather had passed. The apprentice's first lightning lesson draws the same fire down to the fingertips and lets it jump.

spellbook_lightning_bolt.name: Spellbook of Lightning Bolt
spellbook_lightning_bolt.lore: Salmoneus, king of Elis, wanted to be worshipped as Zeus. He drove through his city dragging bronze kettles behind his chariot for thunder and throwing torches for lightning. Zeus answered with the real thing. This tome teaches the real thing: a white line through everything that stands in its path.

spellbook_chain_lightning.name: Spellbook of Chain Lightning
spellbook_chain_lightning.lore: In 1746 the Abbe Nollet linked some two hundred Carthusian monks into one great circle with lengths of iron wire and closed it on a charged Leyden jar. Every monk leapt at the same instant. The spell improves on his experiment. The bolt jumps from one enemy to the next, a little weaker each time.

spellbook_storm_of_vengeance.name: Spellbook of Storm of Vengeance
spellbook_storm_of_vengeance.lore: The Philistines marched on Israel at Mizpah while Samuel was still offering the lamb. The Lord thundered that day with a mighty sound against them and threw them into such confusion that they were routed before a blow was struck. The last storm spell breaks overhead in the same way. All in sight are struck, and many are left stunned.

spellbook_magic_dart.name: Spellbook of Magic Dart
spellbook_magic_dart.lore: The story of William Tell is set in 1307. An Austrian bailiff made him shoot an apple from his own son's head with a crossbow, and he split it. He had kept a second bolt ready for the bailiff. The first spell any apprentice masters is that first bolt: a single dart of force that does not miss.

spellbook_magic_missile.name: Spellbook of Magic Missile
spellbook_magic_missile.lore: Jonathan arranged a signal for his friend David, who was hiding in a field from King Saul. He would shoot three arrows beside a certain stone, and what he called to the boy fetching them would mean stay or run. The spell looses three darts of force together, and none of them needs fetching.

spellbook_force_barrage.name: Spellbook of Force Barrage
spellbook_force_barrage.lore: David refused the king's armour, walked down to the brook, and chose five smooth stones for his shepherd's bag. He needed one. The other four are in this tome. It teaches five darts of force thrown in a breath, and no helmet of bronze has been found that turns them.

spellbook_force_storm.name: Spellbook of Force Storm
spellbook_force_storm.lore: Seven priests carried seven rams' horns around Jericho for seven days, and on the seventh day they went round seven times. Then the people shouted and the wall fell down flat. Nobody had touched it. The spell throws seven darts of pure force, and no wall, shield or ward has turned one yet.

spellbook_annihilation.name: Spellbook of Annihilation
spellbook_annihilation.lore: After the Black Death, painters gave Death a scythe and showed him mowing pope, king and ploughman in the same swath. The harvester takes the ripe ears and bruises the green. This tome teaches his stroke. Creatures already failing are simply gone, and those still strong are cut nearly in half.

spellbook_acid_dart.name: Spellbook of Acid Dart
spellbook_acid_dart.lore: Alchemists made aqua fortis, strong water, by heating saltpetre with vitriol and catching the red fumes. It eats silver and leaves gold, which made it the assayer's friend and the forger's enemy. The apprentice learns to throw a splash of it. The burn goes on working after the splash has landed.

spellbook_acid_arrow.name: Spellbook of Acid Arrow
spellbook_acid_arrow.lore: Roast green vitriol in a sealed retort and a heavy, oily liquid drips from the neck. The alchemists called it oil of vitriol and ranked it first among the acids: poured on cloth it chars, and on flesh it does worse. This tome shapes it into an arrow. The wound keeps eating long after.

spellbook_dissolution.name: Spellbook of Dissolution
spellbook_dissolution.lore: Aqua regia, royal water, is the one acid that dissolves gold. When German troops entered Copenhagen in 1940, the chemist George de Hevesy dissolved two Nobel medals in a jar of it and left the jar on a shelf, where the soldiers ignored it. The gold was recovered and recast after the war. The last acid spell spares nothing.

spellbook_cure_light.name: Spellbook of Cure Light Wounds
spellbook_cure_light.lore: In the Iliad an arrow strikes Menelaus through the belt, and the army sends for Machaon, son of Asclepius. He draws the arrow, sucks the wound clean, and spreads on it the soothing herbs that the centaur Chiron once gave his father. A battlefield primer teaches that much: a small wound, cleaned and closed.

spellbook_cure_wounds.name: Spellbook of Cure Wounds
spellbook_cure_wounds.lore: The Persian physician Ibn Sina, whom Europe called Avicenna, finished his Canon of Medicine in 1025. It filled five books, and universities from Montpellier to Padua still taught from it six hundred years later. Every temple physician's second-year reader is drawn from its pages. It teaches the working cure for an ordinary wound.

spellbook_heal.name: Spellbook of Heal
spellbook_heal.lore: Achilles speared King Telephus in the thigh, and the wound would not close. An oracle said that the wounder would be the healer. Achilles protested that he was no physician, until Odysseus saw the answer: rust scraped from the spear itself, sprinkled in the wound. This tome teaches the major healing word.

spellbook_greater_heal.name: Spellbook of Greater Heal
spellbook_greater_heal.lore: At Epidaurus the sick slept overnight in the hall of Asclepius and waited for the god to come in a dream. Sacred snakes and dogs moved among the sleepers, licking wounds. The cures were carved on stone tablets, and several of the tablets survive. The spell is a whole night there in a moment.

spellbook_resurrection.name: Spellbook of Resurrection
spellbook_resurrection.lore: Lazarus of Bethany had been four days in the tomb when Jesus came, and his sister warned that there would be a smell. Jesus wept, then called him by name in a loud voice. The dead man walked out still wrapped in his grave cloths. This liturgy asks ahead of time. Its caster's next death is refused.

spellbook_sleep.name: Spellbook of Sleep
spellbook_sleep.lore: The shepherd Endymion was so beautiful that the Moon asked Zeus to keep him as he was. He was granted sleep without age or end in a cave on Mount Latmus, and she visits him every night. The gentlest enchantment in the syllabus sends one creature the same way, though far more briefly.

spellbook_mass_sleep.name: Spellbook of Mass Sleep
spellbook_mass_sleep.lore: Saul hunted David with three thousand men and camped on the hill of Hachilah. A deep sleep from the Lord fell on the whole camp. David walked in among them by night, took the spear and the water jug from beside the king's head, and walked out. The spell lays that sleep on every enemy in sight.

spellbook_deep_slumber.name: Spellbook of Deep Slumber
spellbook_deep_slumber.lore: In the tale Charles Perrault printed in 1697, the princess pricks her finger and the good fairy touches everything else in the castle with her wand: guards, cooks, horses, even the spits on the fire with their partridges. All of it stops for a hundred years. The last sleep spell holds a whole room that fast.

spellbook_slow.name: Spellbook of Slow
spellbook_slow.lore: Aesop's hare was so sure of the race that he lay down by the road for a nap. The tortoise never stopped walking. This primer teaches how to trade places with a quick enemy. For a good while the target moves at the tortoise's pace, and the caster is free to be the hare.

spellbook_mass_slow.name: Spellbook of Mass Slow
spellbook_mass_slow.lore: Pharaoh's chariots followed Israel onto the dry bed of the sea. In the morning watch the Lord looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud and clogged their chariot wheels, so that they drove heavily. The charioteers said to one another that it was time to flee. The spell bogs down every enemy in sight.

spellbook_time_freeze.name: Spellbook of Time Freeze
spellbook_time_freeze.lore: Vesuvius buried Pompeii in a day and a night in the year 79. From 1863 Giuseppe Fiorelli poured plaster into the hollows the dead had left in the ash and found them as they were: a man shielding his face, a dog straining at its chain. For a few heartbeats the spell does that to every creature on the floor.

spellbook_hold_monster.name: Spellbook of Hold Monster
spellbook_hold_monster.lore: The gods bound the wolf Fenrir with a ribbon made from six things: the sound of a cat's footfall, a woman's beard, the roots of a mountain, the sinews of a bear, the breath of a fish and the spittle of a bird. None of these exists any longer. The spell ties one creature with a length of it.

spellbook_paralyze.name: Spellbook of Paralyze
spellbook_paralyze.lore: After Baldr's death the gods caught Loki and bound him across three sharp stones in a cave. A serpent drips venom on his face. His wife Sigyn catches it in a bowl, and when she turns to empty the bowl he writhes, and the earth quakes. The stronger binding holds one enemy as fast as that.

spellbook_mass_paralyze.name: Spellbook of Mass Paralyze
spellbook_mass_paralyze.lore: Perseus came home with the Gorgon's head in a bag and found King Polydectes at dinner with his court, still pressing the hero's mother to marry him. Perseus told his friends to cover their eyes and held up the head. The king and his guests are sitting there yet. This tome teaches how to hold a whole room.

spellbook_fear.name: Spellbook of Fear
spellbook_fear.lore: Agamemnon went to war behind a shield with ten rings of bronze, and at its centre the Gorgon glared, with Fear and Rout on either side. Greek soldiers painted her face on shields for centuries. The spell puts that face in front of one enemy, which forgets the fight and runs.

spellbook_terror.name: Spellbook of Terror
spellbook_terror.lore: Gideon took three hundred men against the host of Midian and gave each one a trumpet and a torch hidden in a clay jar. At midnight they smashed the jars, blew the trumpets and shouted. The whole camp woke, cried out and fled. The Word of Terror is that midnight. Every enemy in sight runs.

spellbook_confusion.name: Spellbook of Confusion
spellbook_confusion.lore: Ate, the spirit of folly, walks on the heads of men with soft feet and they do not feel her. She once fooled Zeus himself into a rash oath, and he seized her by the hair and flung her from Olympus for good. She lives among mortals now. The spell sets her on one enemy's shoulders.

spellbook_madness.name: Spellbook of Madness
spellbook_madness.lore: Nebuchadnezzar walked on the roof of his palace and admired the Babylon he had built. That hour his reason left him. He was driven from men and ate grass like an ox, and his hair grew like eagles' feathers, until seven times had passed over him. The Word of Madness breaks every mind in sight.

spellbook_mage_armor.name: Spellbook of Mage Armor
spellbook_mage_armor.lore: Paul wrote to the Ephesians from prison, under Roman guard, and described the kit in front of him piece by piece: belt, breastplate, boots, shield, helmet, sword. He meant truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation and the word. A wizard's first defence is armour as invisible as that. Blows land softer through it.

spellbook_magic_shield.name: Spellbook of Magic Shield
spellbook_magic_shield.lore: Hephaestus made the shield of Achilles in five layers: two of bronze, two of tin and one of gold. The spear of Aeneas drove through two and stopped dead in the gold. This tome teaches how to raise a shield of that make from air. It turns hard blows for a good while.

spellbook_stoneskin.name: Spellbook of Stoneskin
spellbook_stoneskin.lore: Siegfried killed a dragon and bathed in its blood, and his skin grew hard as horn so that no blade could cut it. A linden leaf had stuck between his shoulders, and Hagen learned where. The spell hardens the whole body and lasts longer than any other guard. It leaves no leaf.

spellbook_haste.name: Spellbook of Haste
spellbook_haste.lore: Hermes was born at dawn, invented the lyre by noon, and stole his brother Apollo's cattle by evening. His sandals, the talaria, were golden and winged and carried him over land and sea as fast as the wind. The spell laces them on. For a short while its caster acts twice to an enemy's once.

spellbook_greater_haste.name: Spellbook of Greater Haste
spellbook_greater_haste.lore: Thor's servant Thialfi was the fastest runner among men. In the hall of Utgard-Loki he raced a boy named Hugi three times, and three times Hugi turned at the post before Thialfi reached it. Hugi was the giant king's own thought. This tome teaches a speed nearer to Hugi's, and it lasts.

spellbook_invisibility.name: Spellbook of Invisibility
spellbook_invisibility.lore: Plato tells of the shepherd Gyges, who found a gold ring on a corpse inside a bronze horse in a cleft of the earth. Turned inward on his finger, it made him invisible. He used it to kill the king of Lydia and take the throne. The spell hides its caster until the first blow is struck.

spellbook_greater_invisibility.name: Spellbook of Greater Invisibility
spellbook_greater_invisibility.lore: Siegfried won the Tarnkappe, a cloak of hiding, from the dwarf Alberich. When King Gunther had to beat Queen Brunhild at spear, stone and leap to win her, Siegfried stood unseen beside him and did the work while Gunther made the gestures. This greater spell likewise holds through a fight.

spellbook_displacement.name: Spellbook of Displacement
spellbook_displacement.lore: The poet Stesichorus said that Helen never went to Troy. The gods sent a phantom of her with Paris, and the real Helen waited out the war in Egypt while two armies fought ten years over an image made of cloud. The spell stands such an image beside its caster, and blows go wide.

spellbook_reflect.name: Spellbook of Spell Reflect
spellbook_reflect.lore: Medusa's gaze turned men to stone, so Athena lent Perseus a shield of polished bronze. He walked up to the sleeping Gorgon backward, watching her reflection, and struck without ever looking at her. This tome teaches how to carry the shield. Curses and hostile enchantments are often turned back on their senders.

spellbook_detect_magic.name: Spellbook of Detect Magic
spellbook_detect_magic.lore: The high priest of Israel carried two objects in his breastpiece, the Urim and the Thummim, and by them put questions to God. Nobody now knows what they looked like. They seem to have answered yes or no. This tract asks a like question of each enchanted thing lying in sight: blessed, or cursed?

spellbook_identify.name: Spellbook of Identify
spellbook_identify.lore: King Hiero suspected his goldsmith of mixing silver into a crown and asked Archimedes to prove it without melting the thing. Archimedes saw the answer as his bath overflowed, and ran home shouting that he had found it. What lies in view and what rides in the pack show whether they are blessed or cursed.

spellbook_omnisight.name: Spellbook of Omnisight
spellbook_omnisight.lore: Odin has a high seat called Hlidskjalf, and from it he looks out over all the worlds and understands everything he sees. Two ravens, Thought and Memory, fly out at dawn and report by breakfast. The archmage's sight takes in as much. Things on the floor, in the pack and on the body all show their blessing or their curse.

spellbook_detect_monsters.name: Spellbook of Detect Monsters
spellbook_detect_monsters.lore: The king of Aram surrounded Dothan by night to seize Elisha, and the prophet's servant woke and despaired. Elisha prayed that the young man's eyes be opened. He looked again, and the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire. The spell opens the eyes likewise. Every living thing on the floor shows itself for a while.

spellbook_foresight.name: Spellbook of Foresight
spellbook_foresight.lore: Apollo gave Cassandra of Troy the gift of prophecy, and when she refused him he added a curse: she would always see truly and never be believed. She warned against the wooden horse and was laughed at. The spell gives her sight without her curse. Every creature on the floor is known for a long while.

spellbook_mapping.name: Spellbook of Mapping
spellbook_mapping.lore: Around the year 150 Claudius Ptolemy of Alexandria listed some eight thousand places by latitude and longitude and explained how to draw the round world on a flat sheet. His Geography was lost to the West for a thousand years, and when it returned it remade every chart. The spell plots a whole floor at once.

spellbook_greater_mapping.name: Spellbook of Greater Mapping
spellbook_greater_mapping.lore: The geographer al-Idrisi worked fifteen years at the Norman court of Palermo, questioning every traveller who landed. In 1154 he gave King Roger a map of the world engraved on a silver disc, with a book describing each region. The master's spell is as thorough. Walls, creatures and treasure all appear.

spellbook_blink.name: Spellbook of Blink
spellbook_blink.lore: Philip met an Ethiopian court official on the desert road to Gaza, and baptised him at a roadside pool. When they came up out of the water the Spirit caught Philip away, and he found himself at Azotus, twenty miles off. The first travelling spell works likewise. The destination is not the caster's to choose.

spellbook_phase_door.name: Spellbook of Phase Door
spellbook_phase_door.lore: King Sveigdir of Sweden, the saga says, was walking home drunk at sunset when he saw a dwarf sitting under a boulder as big as a house. The dwarf called to him to come in if he wanted to meet Odin. Sveigdir ran into the stone, it closed, and he never came out. The spell lets its caster come out.

spellbook_gate.name: Spellbook of Gate
spellbook_gate.lore: Jacob slept with a stone for a pillow and dreamed of a ladder set between earth and heaven, with angels going up and down it. He woke afraid and called the place the gate of heaven. Babylon's own name means the gate of God. The spell opens a door of that kind, and a strong ally steps through it.

spellbook_turn_undead.name: Spellbook of Turn Undead
spellbook_turn_undead.lore: The monks' last prayer of the day is Compline, and its old hymn asks the Creator to drive far off the dreams and phantoms of the night. It has been sung at bedtime since at least the seventh century. This compendium gives the words their full weight. The dead in sight are burned by light and flee.

spellbook_sunburst.name: Spellbook of Sunburst
spellbook_sunburst.lore: Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and there his face shone like the sun and his clothes became white as light. The three fell on their faces. Tradition names the mountain Tabor. The greatest of the holy spells borrows a moment of that brightness, and every dead thing in sight is seared and scattered.

spellbook_polymorph.name: Spellbook of Polymorph
spellbook_polymorph.lore: Zeus came to Arcadia disguised as a traveller, and King Lycaon tested his guest's divinity by serving him human flesh. Zeus brought the roof down. Lycaon fled into the fields, tried to speak, and howled: his robes were fur and his arms were legs. The spell remakes one creature, and often into something lesser.

spellbook_mass_polymorph.name: Spellbook of Mass Polymorph
spellbook_mass_polymorph.lore: Leto, carrying her newborn twins, stopped at a pond in Lycia to drink. The peasants cutting reeds there forbade her, and stamped the water into mud for spite. She prayed that they might live in that pond for ever. They are frogs. This tome teaches her prayer: a room full of enemies turned small and feeble.

spellbook_drain_life.name: Spellbook of Drain Life
spellbook_drain_life.lore: Old English called a physician a leech, and gave the worm the same name. Medieval doctors set leeches on patients to draw off bad blood, and France alone imported some forty million a year in the 1830s. The spell reverses the bargain. Life is drawn out of an enemy and into the caster.

spellbook_soul_drain.name: Spellbook of Soul Drain
spellbook_soul_drain.lore: The giant Antaeus challenged every traveller through Libya to wrestle and roofed a temple with the skulls of the losers. His mother was the Earth, and each time he was thrown he rose stronger from her touch. Heracles held him in the air until he weakened. The spell makes an enemy serve as the caster's ground.

spellbook_light.name: Spellbook of Light
spellbook_light.lore: The first words God speaks in Scripture are a command, and in Jerome's Latin they are two words long: fiat lux. Light came before the sun, the moon or anything to see by it. The simplest spell in the library repeats the phrase, and the dark draws back a good distance on every side.

spellbook_knock.name: Spellbook of Knock
spellbook_knock.lore: Ali Baba was cutting wood when forty thieves rode up to a rock face, and their captain said two words. The rock opened. Ali Baba's brother later got in the same way, forgot the words, and tried the name of every other grain he knew. The spell is the right grain. A locked chest close by springs open.

spellbook_cleanse.name: Spellbook of Cleanse
spellbook_cleanse.lore: Naaman, commander of the armies of Aram, was a leper. Elisha did not even come to the door, but sent word to wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman was insulted, since Damascus had better rivers. His servants talked him round, and his flesh came back clean as a child's. One reading lifts one affliction.

spellbook_empower.name: Spellbook of Empower
spellbook_empower.lore: Dying at Roncevaux, Roland tried to break his sword Durendal on a rock so that no enemy would carry it. The sword would not break. High in the Pyrenees there is a gap forty metres wide in the cliff wall, and the mountain people say that was the rock. The spell loads one such stroke into the next blow.

spellbook_levitate.name: Spellbook of Levitate
spellbook_levitate.lore: Joseph of Cupertino, a Franciscan friar who died in 1663, was so slow at his books that he passed for the priesthood only because the examiner asked the one question he knew. At prayer he rose into the air, seventy times before witnesses. He is the patron of examinees. The spell lifts its caster clear of pits and snares.

spellbook_teleport_away.name: Spellbook of Teleport Away
spellbook_teleport_away.lore: Once a year the Athenians could vote to be rid of one citizen. Each man scratched a name on a broken potsherd, an ostrakon, and the winner had ten days to leave the city for ten years. The spell casts the same vote against the nearest enemy, which finds itself elsewhere. With no enemy near, the caster goes instead.

spellbook_smite.name: Spellbook of Smite
spellbook_smite.lore: The Golden Legend tells that a dragon poisoned the countryside of Silene in Libya and was fed first on sheep, then on children chosen by lot. The lot fell on the king's daughter. George rode by, made the sign of the cross, and ran the beast through. The spell is his lance. No hide or ward lessens it.

spellbook_dispel_magic.name: Spellbook of Dispel Magic
spellbook_dispel_magic.lore: An old legend sets Simon the Magician before the emperor in Rome, promising to fly. He leapt from a wooden tower and spirits bore him up over the Forum. The apostle Peter knelt and prayed, the spirits let go, and Simon fell. This tome teaches the prayer's effect. Every enchantment on one enemy drops away.

spellbook_counterspell.name: Spellbook of Counterspell
spellbook_counterspell.lore: The Sirens sang from a meadow heaped with the bones of sailors who had stopped to listen. Odysseus plugged his crew's ears with beeswax and had himself lashed to the mast, so that he alone heard the song and lived. The spell is wax and rope together. Charms, terrors and confusions slide off its caster for a time.

spellbook_summon_guardian.name: Spellbook of Summon Guardian
spellbook_summon_guardian.lore: A lion limped into Jerome's monastery at Bethlehem, and the monks ran. Jerome looked at the paw, drew out a thorn, and dressed the wound. The lion stayed for the rest of its life and was set to guarding the monastery's donkey. The spell calls a beast of that loyalty, though not always a lion.

spellbook_disintegrate.name: Spellbook of Disintegrate
spellbook_disintegrate.lore: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a statue with a head of gold, a chest of silver, thighs of bronze and feet of iron mixed with clay. A stone cut by no human hand struck the feet, and the whole figure became chaff that the wind carried off. The spell throws that stone. Half the time, nothing is left.

spellbook_power_word_kill.name: Spellbook of Power Word Kill
spellbook_power_word_kill.lore: The legends of the golem say that its maker wrote the Hebrew word emet, truth, on its brow, and the clay stood up. To end it he rubbed out one letter. What remained was met: dead. This tome holds the shorter word. Spoken at a creature already weakened enough, it is the last thing heard.

spellbook_wish.name: Spellbook of Wish
spellbook_wish.lore: Midas asked that all he touched turn to gold, and nearly starved. The Sibyl of Cumae asked for as many years as she held grains of sand and forgot to ask for youth. She shrank until she lived in a jar and wanted only to die. This tome has one blank page. Reality picks the boon, which is safer.

spellbook_imprisonment.name: Spellbook of Imprisonment
spellbook_imprisonment.lore: In the Arabian Nights a fisherman hauls up a copper jar stopped with lead and stamped with the seal of Solomon. He pries it open, and smoke pours out and becomes a jinni who has sat inside for eighteen hundred years. The spell is the stopper. One enemy is shut in stone for a very long time.

spellbook_banishment.name: Spellbook of Banishment
spellbook_banishment.lore: There was war in heaven. Michael and his angels fought the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back and did not prevail, and no place was found for them there any longer. The spell repeats the verdict on a small scale. A demon, fey or spirit is sent back where it came from.

spellbook_army_of_darkness.name: Spellbook of Army of Darkness
spellbook_army_of_darkness.lore: The warriors Odin gathers in Valhalla are the Einherjar, men who fell in battle. Every morning they arm and cut one another down in the yard, and every evening they rise whole and go in to supper. This tome borrows the idea and none of the honour. Five of the dead get up and fight for the caster.

necronomicon.name: The Necronomicon
necronomicon.unidentified_name: a book bound in human flesh
necronomicon.lore: H. P. Lovecraft swore he made it up. In his stories of the 1920s it is the work of the mad poet Abdul Alhazred, who wrote it at Damascus under the title Al Azif and was later eaten alive by something invisible in a marketplace. Librarians have been asked for it ever since. The copy bound here in something that is not calfskin disagrees with him. It should not be read aloud, and the dead know when it is.

sefer_yetzirah.name: Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Formation)
sefer_yetzirah.lore: The Sefer Yetzirah, the Book of Formation, is a few pages long and among the oldest books of Jewish mysticism. Tradition gives it to Abraham. It teaches that God made the world with thirty-two paths of wisdom: the ten numbers and the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet. A legend of Prague says the great Rabbi Loew used its letters to raise a man of clay to guard the ghetto. Whoever learns its working raises a guardian too.

picatrix.name: Picatrix
picatrix.lore: Its Arabic title is Ghayat al-Hakim, the Aim of the Sage. It was compiled in Muslim Spain, and in 1256 King Alfonso the Wise of Castile had it put into Spanish and then Latin, under the name Picatrix. For four centuries scholars read it quietly. It teaches how to draw the powers of the planets down into carved images. This working draws on Mars, and every enemy in sight burns.

lemegeton.name: Lemegeton (The Lesser Key of Solomon)
lemegeton.unidentified_name: a black tome sealed with sigils
lemegeton.lore: The Lemegeton, or Lesser Key of Solomon, is five books bound as one. The first, the Ars Goetia, lists seventy-two spirits that King Solomon is said to have shut in a vessel of brass, each with a seal, a rank and a use. Bael makes men invisible, Vassago finds what is lost, and all of them are liars. Samuel Mathers translated it and Aleister Crowley printed it in 1904. What answers its call in this place is the dead: five of them.

book_of_thoth.name: Book of Thoth
book_of_thoth.unidentified_name: a heavy book bound in papyrus and gold
book_of_thoth.lore: A book of a book of a book. Thoth hid it at the bottom of the Nile in a box of iron in a box of bronze in a box of ebony in a box of ivory in a box of silver in a box of gold, and a serpent that cannot die was set to guard it. To read it once is to know everything the world holds today; to read it wrong is to lose the pieces you had.
